newsitem.title: ICELAND: Icelanders brace for flooding after volcano.
newsitem.headline: Icelanders brace for flooding after volcano.

text.p: Icelanders built causeways on Friday as they braced themselves for massive flooding following a volcanic eruption under a glacier in the south of Iceland.
Emergency teams were toiling round the clock on preparations to prevent the expected huge flows of water from wrecking bridges, roads and power stations.
Parts of the southern Icelandic coast were closed to traffic as water levels in lakes under the glacier rose to their highest levels this century.

"We are waiting for the floods to start," Ragnar Stefansson, head of Iceland's Meteorological Institute's geophysics department, told Reuters. "And the longer the wait, the bigger the floods are going to be when they start."

On Wednesday the volcano smashed through the Vatnajokull glacier, which is six hundred metres (yards) thick in some places and covers about one-tenth of Iceland, at a point about 190 km (120 miles) east of Reykjavik.
It spewed black clouds into the air, some seven kms (five miles) high, forming a sulphur-smelling tower of ash which was visible from most parts of Iceland.
Occasional bursts of red lightning lit up the air over the 10-km long fissure.
Although no human settlements were near the source of the eruption, geologists said there was a risk of contamination from the ash, which contained poisonous flourides.
The eruption has been accompanied by volcanic tremors, some registering over four points on the Richter scale, but those had died down recently.
Air traffic controllers said many airlines had requested permission to fly over the eruption to show passengers.
